title: Angels giving permission
hookLine: the blessing pictures angels granting each other permission before they praise

lines: A CROWD THAT DOES IT PERFECTLY.
cards: Two people in a meeting start talking at once, and both push on. Somebody else waits for a gap that never comes. Getting a group to speak with one voice is hard.
In the middle of the first blessing before the Shema, the prayer book pulls back a curtain on heaven and shows a crowd doing it perfectly. Not because they're loud or fast.
Because, before anyone says a word, they give each other permission.

teach.b: The scene borrows from the prophet Isaiah's vision. In the old Jewish translation: "And one called unto another, and said: Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory."
One called unto another. The prayer book reads that line closely and paints it out. The angels all take upon themselves the yoke of heaven's kingdom, one from another.
And they give permission, reshut, one to another, to sanctify their Creator.
Then they speak with a calm spirit, with clear speech, with a holy melody, all as one: holy, holy, holy. Where did the idea of permission come from?
The old Aramaic translation of Isaiah, the Targum, renders one called unto another as they receive from one another. The prayer book builds on readings like that. So even angels don't simply start.
Each one waits, offers the others room, and accepts the call from someone else.
The holiness comes after the courtesy.
Then a second group of angels answers with a line from Ezekiel: blessed be the glory of the LORD from its place.
Some authorities allow this angel scene to be said even by someone praying alone, because it describes heaven's praise rather than making the congregation's own call.
Its picture is a choir where nobody grabs the first note.

how: The angel scene inside Yotzer Or, sometimes called the Kedushah of the blessing, is said each morning before the Shema; it is often said seated, with people joining in aloud at holy, holy, holy and blessed be the glory.

games.q: you're one of the angels in the prayer book's scene, about to praise God. what do you do first?
o: sing the first note before anyone else.
give the others permission, and accept it from them.
wait until everyone else has finished.
games.why: they all take the yoke one from another, and give reshut, permission, one to another. then they say holy, holy, holy, all as one.

practice: Think of a conversation coming up, a meeting, a dinner, a call with someone you sometimes talk over, and picture the moment you'd usually jump in.
Now picture pausing instead and asking, can I add something, or turning to the quiet person: what do you think? Calm spirit, clear speech.

wordCard.voice: Reshut. Permission, leave — the word for how angels, in Yotzer Or, give each other room before they call out holy, holy, holy.

orig.note: Hebrew: permission, leave. the angels give it one to another.

carryVoice: Your line: they give each other leave. Even angels wait their turn. See you tomorrow.
